summary: Accepted the beneficiary relationship from AI infrastructure and power bottlenecks to GE Vernova with high positive sensitivity and medium confidence. Current Q2 2026 evidence shows direct transmission through Power and Electrification demand, data-centre orders, backlog, margins, and cash generation, while project schedules, customer concentration, backlog quality, working-capital normalization, Wind execution, capacity investment, acquisition integration, and adverse current valuation limit shareholder transmission. Updated the relationship page, catalog, log, and canonical relationship row; no strategy or follow-up operation was created because the maintained base case offers only 1.9% upside and does not meet the margin-of-safety gate.

evidence.claim: GE Vernova's SEC-filed Q2 2026 Form 10-Q confirms strong Power and Electrification demand and cash generation; at June 30 it reported USD 13.1 billion cash, USD 2.794 billion long-term borrowings, USD 9.897 billion first-half free cash flow, 266.3 million period-end shares, and 270 million Q2 diluted weighted-average shares, while working-capital dependence, Wind execution, tariffs, capacity investment, acquisition integration, and backlog conversion remain material risks.

The maintained GE Vernova review records Q2 orders of USD 24.2 billion, USD 176 billion total backlog, more than USD 5 billion of year-to-date data-centre orders, 116 GW of gas-equipment backlog and slot reservations, an 11.3% adjusted EBITDA margin, and strong cash conversion, alongside a USD 996.57 mark and bounded downside and base values of USD 804.84 and USD 1,015.95.

The maintained idea defines the causal channel from concentrated data-centre electricity demand through generation, grid, interconnection, and electrical-equipment bottlenecks to qualified supplier orders, margins, and cash, with project delays, customer concentration, capacity additions, demand normalization, and valuation as explicit counterweights.

daily_report_items: Accepted the medium-confidence, high-sensitivity positive beneficiary relationship from AI infrastructure and power bottlenecks to GE Vernova based on Power and Electrification demand, data-centre orders, backlog, margins, and cash generation; no strategy follow-up was created because working-capital normalization, execution risks, and current valuation remain limiting.
